questions.q: In a fraud model, what is a false negative?
options: A genuine transaction flagged as fraud
A fraudulent transaction the model did not flag
A genuine transaction correctly passed
A fraud correctly flagged
questions.why: "Negative" is the prediction (not fraud) and "false" means it was wrong, so it is a missed fraud. A genuine transaction flagged as fraud is the other mistake, a false positive or false alarm.

questions.q: In a loan dataset, 3% of borrowers default. What accuracy does a "model" score if it predicts "no default" for everyone?
questions.why: It is right for every non-defaulter: **97%** accuracy, while catching no defaults at all (recall 0%). This is why accuracy misleads on imbalanced data; 3% is the default rate, not the accuracy.

questions.q: A churn model has TP = 30, FP = 20 and FN = 10. What is its F1 score?
options: About 0.675
About 0.667
questions.why: Precision = 30 / 50 = 0.60; recall = 30 / 40 = 0.75; F1 = 2 × 0.6 × 0.75 / (0.6 + 0.75) = 0.9 / 1.35 ≈ **0.667**. 0.675 is the ordinary average of precision and recall; F1 is the harmonic mean, which sits slightly closer to the lower value.

questions.q: After a change to the model's settings, precision falls from 70% to 55% and recall rises from 60% to 85%. What most likely changed?
options: The decision threshold was raised
The decision threshold was lowered, so more cases are flagged: more real positives caught, but more false alarms
The model was retrained on more data
The test set became more balanced
questions.why: Lowering the threshold makes the alarm more sensitive: recall goes up and precision usually goes down. Raising it does the opposite. The threshold is a business decision and moves you along this trade-off without changing the model itself.

questions.q: A model has precision 1.0 and recall 0.02. What is its F1, and why?
options: 0.51, the average of the two
0.02, because F1 equals the lower value
1.0, because precision is perfect
About 0.039, because the harmonic mean stays low when either value is low
questions.why: F1 = 2 × 1.0 × 0.02 / (1.0 + 0.02) ≈ **0.039**. The ordinary average, 0.51, sounds respectable for a model that catches only 2% of positives; the harmonic mean refuses to be rescued by one strong number. It is close to, but not exactly, the lower value.

questions.q: A missed defect (FN) costs ₹10,000 and a false alarm (FP) costs ₹1,000. Model A has FN 20 and FP 100; Model B has FN 5 and FP 300. Which is cheaper?
options: Model A, at ₹3,00,000 against ₹3,50,000
Model B, at ₹3,50,000 against ₹3,00,000
Model B, because it has fewer misses
They cost the same
questions.why: A: 20 × ₹10,000 + 100 × ₹1,000 = ₹3,00,000. B: 5 × ₹10,000 + 300 × ₹1,000 = ₹3,50,000. Higher recall is not automatically better: here the extra 200 false alarms cost more than the 15 misses saved. When costs are known, let the rupees decide.

questions.q: scikit-learn's `confusion_matrix(y_true, y_pred)` returns [[900, 30], [20, 50]]. What is the precision for the positive class?
questions.why: Rows are actual and columns are predicted, ordered [0, 1], so `ravel()` gives TN 900, FP 30, FN 20, TP 50. Precision = TP / (TP + FP) = 50 / 80 = **0.625**. 0.714 is recall (50 / 70), which you get by reading the matrix the wrong way round; 0.95 is accuracy.

questions.q: Interview: "Your fraud model has ROC-AUC 0.97 but the operations team says most alerts are false. How can both be true?" Which answer is best?
options: With very rare positives, the huge number of true negatives keeps the false positive rate small, so ROC-AUC looks flattering; even a small FPR can mean far more false alarms than frauds. Look at the precision–recall curve (PR-AUC) and choose the threshold by cost
They cannot; a high AUC guarantees high precision
The team is using the wrong threshold of 0.5, which AUC does not allow
ROC-AUC measures accuracy, which is high on imbalanced data
questions.why: ROC-AUC uses the false positive rate, FP / (FP + TN), which stays tiny when negatives vastly outnumber positives. Precision compares false alarms with true catches, which is what the team experiences. AUC ignores the threshold rather than forbidding one.
